question: A team wants a refactoring agent to automatically improve a file's structure once edits are auto-approved, but they also want a record of every modified file path written to an append-only log immediately after each change lands on disk. Which hook should run the logging logic, and at which point?
options: A) A SessionEnd hook, since it only runs once when the entire session terminates rather than after each individual file change
B) A PreToolUse hook matched to Edit and Write, since it runs before the tool executes and the change has not yet landed on disk
C) A UserPromptSubmit hook, since it fires when the user submits a prompt rather than after a file modification occurs
D) A PostToolUse hook matched to Edit and Write, since it runs after the tool has executed and the change has already landed on disk
correct_answers: D) A PostToolUse hook matched to Edit and Write, since it runs after the tool has executed and the change has already landed on disk
explanations: Incorrect. SessionEnd fires once at session termination, not after each individual file change, so it would not produce a per-change log.
Incorrect. PreToolUse runs before the tool executes, so the file change would not yet be on disk when the log entry is written.
Incorrect. UserPromptSubmit fires on prompt submission, unrelated to when a file modification actually occurs.
Correct. PostToolUse hooks run after the matched tool executes, so by the time the hook fires the edit has already landed on disk, matching the requirement to log after the change lands.
